title: tenant-sla-escrow-and-event-driven-soft-burst-attenuator
author: Priya Nandakumar
release_notes: Adds a per-tenant SLA escrow mechanism and an event-driven soft-burst attenuator to improve SLA stability under microbursts; includes telemetry for utilization-drift reporting and a gradual rollout plan to Dedicated clusters.
description:
Context: Customers running Dedicated pools reported intermittent SLA violations during microburst traffic patterns where short-lived tenant spikes caused headroom starvation for higher-priority tenants. Existing reservation logic is conservative (static safety margins) and leads to both wasteful over-reservation and brittle underprovisioning during sudden surges. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) a per-tenant SLA escrow that holds a small, timeboxed credit buffer for high-priority tenants and 2) an event-driven soft-burst attenuator that temporarily reduces burst acceptance for lower-priority traffic when escrow levels are low.
Goals: stabilize latency SLAs for high-priority tenants, reduce permanent over-reservation, and surface utilization drift signals for ops.
Design summary: the SLA escrow implements a compact ledger per tenant: escrow credits are accumulated from unused reservation delta and a small periodic accrual (configurable). Credits have expiry windows and are consumed when tenant latency percentiles threaten configured SLO thresholds. The soft-burst attenuator is an admission-time policy module that consults escrow state and pool utilization signals; instead of hard rejection, it applies probabilistic acceptance and adaptive concurrency caps to low-priority requests, smoothing admission without dropping in-flight work.
Telemetry: new metrics (tenant_escrow_credits, tenant_escrow_expiry_rate, attenuator_reject_rate, attenuator_prob_accept, pool_utilization_drift_percentile) plus tracing hooks around admission decisions.
Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, start with sampling on 10% of Dedicated pools, graduate after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and no observed regression in 95th latency for flagged tenants.
Backcompat: default escrow accrual is zero and attenuator is disabled; no breaking changes to API.
Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for escrow ledger and expiry logic - [x] Integration tests simulating microburst scenarios in bench/lab - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts (ops) - [x] Feature flag + staged rollout doc - [x] Docs: ops/tenant-reservations.md updated
Commits: - "implement: lightweight tenant escrow ledger and config plumbing" - "feature: event-driven soft-burst attenuator and admission adapter" - "telemetry: add utilization-drift reporter and new escrow metrics" - "tests: unit and integ microburst scenarios"
Files changed (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/escrow_ledger.go (core escrow accounting and expiry) - controllers/allocator/tenant_priority_allocator.go (hook into admission path, consult escrow) - pkg/autoscaler/soft_burst_attenuator.go (probabilistic admission, concurrency caps) - telemetry/utilization_reporter.go (drift percentiles and pool-sampling) - charts/dedicated/values.yaml (feature flag and conservative defaults) - docs/ops/tenant-reservations.md (operational runbook and rollout instructions) - tests/integration/microburst_escrow_test.go (bench harness scenarios)
Compatibility notes: the escrow ledger stores small state in existing per-tenant metadata objects; it uses existing migration-safe keyed entries and defaults to empty for older clusters. No changes to external APIs.
Observability: added per-tenant and per-pool metrics described above and a Grafana dashboard json (ops only).
Performance: escrow accounting uses lock-free counters where possible and only samples heavy-weight checks on admission to keep p95 admission latency increase < 0.5ms in benchmarked scenarios.
Security & privacy: escrow values are non-sensitive and stored in cluster control-plane DB; no user data is logged.
Testing summary: unit coverage for ledger expiry and accrual paths, integration runs in benchmark-lab show median p99 latency drop for priority tenants in 3/3 simulated microburst patterns when feature enabled.
Migration & rollback: feature flag off = no behavior change. If regressions detected, operator can toggle off immediately and the allocator falls back to previous reservation flow.
Related work: builds on ENG-2319 (reservation accounting refactor) and complements ENG-2401 (pool utilization sampler). Links: linear/ENG-2319, linear/ENG-2401, incident/SUP-5421
